NISAR maps 243 ha of water, Sentinel-1 418 ha; 146 ha only on NISAR's map, 320 ha only on Sentinel-1's.

soil.title: Soil wetness before the storm
soil.what: NISAR soil moisture of the top soil (L3 SME2, a provisional product, not yet validated), as stored for the spatial model by pipeline/soil_moisture.py: every pass over the site, the passes of one day averaged, on 200 m cells. The last dates before the DANA of 18 to 19 Oct; dates are compared on the cells both have.
caption: 16 Oct, two days before the storm: half of the land read below 0.21 m³/m³ of soil moisture, nine in ten cells below 0.23.
Of the 17 earlier dates, from 18 Jun on, 3 read drier on the same cells.
Over the ground that then flooded (the 681 cells touching the Copernicus EMS outline) it read 0.18, the rest of the land 0.21.
The ground was not soaked when the storm came: it was among the driest readings of the season.

Water goes from 74 ha on 29 Aug to 578 ha on 28 Oct.
On 4 of the 11 passes an optical satellite saw less than half of the land clear within a day.
